To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV‐1 and HIV‐2 fusion is mediated by different envelope glycoprotein complexes, and that the HIV‐1 envelope is sensitive to cytochalasin‐induced disruption of the actin cytoskeleton.
the HIV‐1 and HIV‐2 envelope proteins mediate fusion of HeLa cells with HeLa‐target cells at 37°C.
HIV‐1 and HIV‐2 envelope‐mediated membrane fusion are differentially affected by temperature, Ca2+, and cytochalasins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in HIV‐1 and HIV‐2 envelope‐mediated fusion.
the study of the mechanisms of HIV‐1 and HIV‐2 envelope mediated cell fusion.
the development of novel strategies for the treatment of HIV‐1 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are differences in the fusion mechanisms of HIV‐1 and HIV‐2, but these differences are subtle and may be due to the different cell lines used.
the fusion process mediated by the HIV‐2 envelope is more sensitive to the experimental conditions tested, whereas HIV‐ 1 fusion is more sensitive to cytochalasin and Ca2+ ions.
the HIV‐2 envelope protein‐mediated fusion is not dependent on Ca2+ or cytochalasin, whereas HIV‐I envelope glycoprotein is dependent on Ca2+, but not on cytochalasin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV‐2 fusion is more sensitive to temperature than HIV‐1 and that HIV‐1 fusion requires Ca2+, but not dynamic actin cytoskeleton, whereas HIV‐2 fusion does not.
HIV‐1 fusion requires a temperature of ≥31°C and Ca2+ in addition to the cytoskeleton, whereas HIV‐2 fusion occurs at temperatures ≥25° and in the absence of cytoskeleton or Ca2+.
HIV‐2 fusion is Ca2+ independent and is mediated by a mechanism that does not require cytoskeletal rearrangement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fusion process mediated by HIV‐2 envelope is more similar to the fusion mediated by the retrovirus murine leukaemia virus, whereas the fusion mediated by HIV‐1 is more similar to that of the retrovirus Moloney murine leukaemic virus.
